decisions.subject: FK edges into excluded tables (1460 census relationships)
decisions.decision: Tables in the shared_postgresql and orm_framework buckets (table_buckets.json, 379 excluded via --exclude-table) stay in PostgreSQL. Every FK column from a migrated collection into one of them (create_uid, write_uid, company_id, currency_id, partner_id, ...) remains a plain integer field holding the PostgreSQL id, resolved by the ORM across stores; edges between two excluded tables are not modeled. model_patch.py --check at 9a584b4 still reports these edges as 'no rationale row' because it consults modeling.excluded (the exclude decision) and not modeling.excluded_tables (the proposer's --exclude-table list): reported as a plugin gap on UNT12-9, not patched.

decisions.subject: kpi_provider.get_kpi_summary runs without a registry (NOTES.md s2.3 row 23, blocked)
decisions.decision: Model-side answer: no spec change. The KPI query reads account_move.state, account_move.review_state, account_move.journal_id, account_move.statement_line_id, account_journal.type and account_bank_statement_line.is_reconciled; all six stay top-level fields of the accountMove, accountJournal and accountBankStatementLine collections (none is embedded), so the HTTP-layer endpoint can run the same filters as one aggregation on accountMove with $lookup on accountJournal and accountBankStatementLine, no registry needed. The information_schema probe that guards it becomes a check that the three collections exist. Until that rewrite ships, the endpoint returns [] (its own 'module not installed' path) once account_move leaves PostgreSQL; the PG id shadow cannot serve it because it has no state/journal columns.

decisions.subject: stock post_init_hook reads product_product.qty_available raw (NOTES.md s2.3 row 28, blocked)
decisions.decision: Model-side answer: no spec change, an ordering rule for the plan. _create_inventory_adjustment reads the pre-stock stored JSONB column product_product.qty_available at `-i stock` time only. The rule: on every database that can install stock, stock is installed before product_product opts into MongoDB (fresh installs: `-i stock` before the product unit migrates; existing databases already have stock), so the hook always finds the column in PostgreSQL. This order must hold without exception: once product_product is Mongo-backed its PostgreSQL shadow keeps id only, the hook's SELECT fails with `column qty_available does not exist` (it does not return an empty result), and `-i stock` aborts. If the wave plan cannot guarantee the order, row 28 stays blocked and the storage-path wave owns a rewrite of the hook (detect a Mongo-backed product_product and skip or read the stored quantities from the product documents); that is ORM code and is not written here. The productProduct collection does not need a qty_available field: with stock installed the field is computed from stock_quant.
